text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday met Algeria's President Liamine Zeroual to discuss the stalled Middle East peace process, Algerian state-run radio said.
"He briefed President Zeroual in the light of the Israelis' stubbornness to block the peace process," the radio said.
After his brief visit Arafat left, probably for Cairo, said the radio, without giving further details.
Arafat on Tuesday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of plotting to "pulverise" the Middle East peace process.

He told reporters after meeting Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali in Tunis: "I have fully informed the president about the obstacles the Israeli prime minister is putting in the way of the peace process with the aim of freezing it. There is a plot to pulverise the peace process".
Israeli-Palestinian peace moves ground to a halt in March after Israel starting building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"Jerusalem is facing an Israeli attack to Judaise it. I appeal our Arab and Moslem nation to defend (East) Jerusalem because this is not only a Palestinian cause, but also an Arab, Moslem and Christian cause," he said.
Israeli-Palestinian violence raged again in the West Bank and Gaza on Wednesday.

Israeli soldiers shot dead a Palestinian teenager in Gaza during protests over Jewish settlement expansion and dozens of Arabs were wounded in the West Bank town of Hebron. A top PLO official warned of impending disaster unless peace was pursued.
